decision_reason: This is a documented Turing research artifact demonstrating retrieval-augmented reasoning over content scraped from NHS A-to-Z condition pages. Its README attributes the work to the Turing's t0 research initiative; the use of NHS web content is not evidence that NHS commissioned, funded, authored or stewards this repository. Reject for absent public-agency provenance despite a public MIT license and exact research paper.

government_provenance.note: The README calls `t0` a research initiative at the Alan Turing Institute and says the example content is taken from NHS A-to-Z webpages. No NHS or other public-body role in creating, commissioning, funding or stewarding this software is identified; use of public NHS web content is not sponsorship.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository exposes application and RAG code, tests, training/deployment scripts, data-ingestion workflow and setup instructions without credentials.

primary_evidence.note: The exact research report documents the t0-1 retrieval-augmented reasoning experiment; the repository provides the code and detailed local setup/serving and query guidance. This is scholarly evidence for the Turing research artifact, not evidence of NHS deployment or sponsorship.

product_identity: t0-1, a Turing research demonstration/application of retrieval-augmented reasoning over NHS public condition webpages using lean language models; not an NHS product or service.
agency: No public body relationship evidenced; NHS content is used as source material only
status_note: The root initial commit in March 2025 includes source and MIT license. Repo README describes NHS A-to-Z pages as a domain-specific data corpus and names Turing's t0 initiative; no institutional NHS relationship was asserted.

decision_reason: TEA Techniques is a separately identified, self-standing web application: an interactive catalogue/wizard for responsible-AI assurance methods. Its own project-information page reports exact support from EPSRC CVDNet, UKRI's BRAID programme and UKRI's Trustworthy Autonomous Hub; the Alan Turing Institute's official TEA page links this exact repo/live site and marks the application publicly available in beta. The code is public under a complete MIT license, and its first repository commit in July 2025 added substantive application source, documentation and that license together. The user-facing site and README give concrete browse/search/wizard guidance. This review does not claim that this specific component was externally deployed by a named partner; the supported pathway is an officially distributed, documented public-beta tool.

government_provenance.note: The exact TEA Techniques project-info page states this component received EPSRC CVDNet project support from October 2024 to present, UKRI BRAID funding March-September 2024, and UKRI Trustworthy Autonomous Hub funding (Grant TAS_PP_00040) July 2021-June 2022. The Alan Turing Institute is the host/developer; it is not represented as a government agency.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository exposes the complete web application, data and schema, tests, build configuration, MCP/knowledge-graph implementation and user documentation without credentials. The separate live app is linked from the Turing project page.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE contains a complete MIT grant. GitHub API history shows the first commit on 2025-07-28 added this license alongside the complete functional application, data, user-facing README and docs; it was not a license-only commit. Commit: https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/tea-techniques/commit/0483fa7efd4a43c9777b13e0112f3efd6bed6595.

primary_evidence.note: The official Turing TEA page describes TEA Techniques as a self-standing application with an interactive catalogue of more than 100 responsible-AI techniques, links its exact live site and repository, and marks it publicly available in beta. The repo and live site's project-information/user guide explain browsing, filtering and using the Technique Finder Wizard. No specific external deployment/use is claimed for this component.

product_identity: TEA Techniques, a self-standing Turing web application for browsing and discovering responsible-AI assurance techniques; distinct from the interoperating TEA Platform web application, though able to serve as its plugin/component.
agency: UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), via EPSRC CVDNet, UKRI BRAID, and the UKRI Trustworthy Autonomous Hub; The Alan Turing Institute is the host/developer
family_note: The official Turing page identifies TEA Platform, TEA Techniques, and TEA Evidence as three interoperating but distinct components; it explicitly calls Techniques a self-standing application. Preserve that product boundary and do not substitute the AssurancePlatform repository/license for this codebase.
status_note: Repository first published licensed source on 2025-07-28. The cited first commit added the app, MIT license, user README and documentation together. Current TEA project page describes the Techniques app as public beta, not a government production deployment; no external partner use of this exact component is asserted.
